elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice
elements.evidence: "upon at least ninety (90) days' written notice to M&I"

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on such termination
elements.evidence: "M&I shall refund to Customer any prepaid Fees attributable to the period after the Effective Date of Termination"

elements.element: No early-termination fee payable by Customer (preferred exit is fee-free)
elements.evidence: "provided that Customer pays M&I an early termination fee ... not to exceed three (3) times the Monthly Base Fee"

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during the committed term
elements.evidence: "10.2 Partial Termination by M&I. M&I may, at any time, withdraw any of the Services (other than the Core Services) upon providing ninety (90) days' prior written notice" (untouched)

elements.element: Customer termination right on 60–90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "Customer may terminate this Agreement during the Term upon at least ninety (90) days' written notice to M&I"

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "in an amount not to exceed three (3) times the Monthly Base Fee in effect as of the Effective Date of Termination"

elements.element: Vendor convenience termination permitted only effective at the end of a term
elements.evidence: No end-of-term restriction inserted; "M&I may, at any time, withdraw any of the Services ... upon providing ninety (90) days' prior written notice" remains, and Section 10.2 was not amended

elements.element: Vendor convenience termination requires 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: Section 10.2 gives "ninety (90) days' prior written notice" for Service withdrawal, but no express Vendor agreement-level convenience-termination notice provision appears in the excerpt

offending_extra_words: M&I shall refund to Customer any prepaid Fees attributable to the period after the Effective Date of Termination
The Termination for Convenience Fee shall be paid to M&I within thirty (30) days following the Effective Date of Termination.
reasons: Fallback is incomplete: the redline does not restrict M&I's convenience termination to the end of the then-current term, and Section 10.2 still lets M&I withdraw non-Core Services "at any time" mid-term. Add an express sentence that M&I may terminate for convenience only effective at the end of the then-current Term on 90 days' notice.
Preferred is not met (90 days rather than 30 days' notice and a fee remains), so the clause cannot be scored at the preferred level.

Minimality fails: the drafter imported a preferred-level protection (pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees) into a fallback-locked edit, and additionally rewrote the payment-timing sentence, deleted the recoverable "reasonable Expenses" and "or other costs" language, and deleted the Section 13.4 carve-out sentence. The fallback needed only the notice figure and a capped fee.
A whole-paragraph replacement was used where changing "one (1) years'" to "ninety (90) days'" and replacing the fee formula with the 3-month cap would suffice.
Note (non-blocking): the "Estimated Remaining Value" definition in clause N is now potentially orphaned in this excerpt; confirm it is still used elsewhere or leave the definition untouched, as done.
